title: Data Sovereignty and Privacy
summary: Individuals own and selectively share their data through privacy-centric vaults, dynamic consent, and context-aware controls.
webProblem: Data is harvested and locked away
opportunity: Individuals own and selectively share their data

hero.headline: Your data should work for you, not against you.
hero.text: Today, personal information is harvested as the price of participation. Data sovereignty restores control: you decide what is stored, shared, and revoked across contexts.

problemStory.title: Why this matters
problemStory.scenario: A health app sells behavioral data to advertisers. A school platform keeps student records after graduation. Leaving a service rarely means taking your history with you, or deleting it for good.

webLimitations.title: Why today's Web struggles
webLimitations.text: Services store user data as a competitive asset. Interoperability of identity and history threatens that advantage, so sovereignty is treated as a compliance checkbox rather than a design goal.

futureVision.title: Imagine instead
futureVision.text: Personal data vaults and selective disclosure let you prove what is needed without surrendering everything else.
